title: Normalized derived signed-line reduction comparisons
statement: Fix the data l,E,X,L,b of [def-pur-integral-line-reduction-data], where L has rank one and b satisfies PowerFormula. There exist natural isomorphisms d(m,n) from ordinary(L,m) followed by derived scalar reduction n to derived scalar reduction n followed by finiteOrdinary(L,n,m). They satisfy DerivedFormula for every good representative: the balancing ChainFormula, the equality with d through the actual reduction counit and actual tensor representative isomorphisms, and the strict quotient-transition square with TransitionFormula. This statement has no assertion about cohomological support or its intervals.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), specializing to the coefficient quotient; first proof step of lem-pur-integral-line-derived-comparisons

proof.text: Apply line_unbounded_derived_tensor to each signed integral and finite line: their degree-zero complexes are K-flat and tensoring with them is computed termwise. Apply canonical tensor pullback to the identity topos and the actual quotient ring map, using the given ordinary and derived scalar functors and the published tensor representative models. Whisker the natural derived tensor comparison with the fixed degree-zero signed line, then compose the second tensor factor with the image of b under the single-complex functor and Q. These are the required natural isomorphisms d.

source.place: Tags 06YU and 07A4, quotient map on the same ringed topos

proof.text: On a good representative use the chain tensor comparison and the canonical scalar-extension/single-complex isomorphism, followed by b on the line factor. Its summand of bidegree (i,0) sends c tensor (x tensor y) to (c tensor x) tensor b(1 tensor y), which is ChainFormula. The canonical pullback representative square, together with the actual reduction counit and the defining tensor model isomorphisms, gives exactly the DerivedFormula representative equation after cancellation of inverse comparisons.

Define the finite transition by conjugating the existing strict scalar-reduction transition through the chain comparisons. To check TransitionFormula, evaluate locally on pure tensor generators. Both routes apply the same quotient homomorphism to the first scalar; on the line factor powerTransition is defined by conjugating that same transition through b. Additivity, tensor balancing and sheafification extend the equality to all sections. The conjugation definition gives the strict square by cancellation. These choices satisfy all three clauses of DerivedFormula simultaneously.
